dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: Hello there. Is anything the matter? I can help you with it — so long as it doesn't involve performances.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there something wrong with performances?

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: Not that, per se. I'm just not all that interested in operas, plays, or magic, and the like.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I was only sent here because when asked "do you like theater?" I answered "no."

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: I suppose they don't want Gardes posted here to be distracted by performances or trials. We do need to focus on work, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine at the moment, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: They've made big changes in how they publicize the performances and trials as if they're trying to differentiate more between them. That's a good thing, for me at least.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A trial that looks like a performance?

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: It's just a metaphor. Since the Hydro Archon would be present, we usually add some dramatic elements, like those found in plays.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: But the trials themselves are legitimate. Thanks to the Chief Justice and Oratrice's just verdict, every trial will come to a successful conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: Um, it seems that Lady Furina has left the Palais Mermonia and no longer involves herself in trials.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: Oops, I guess it's easy to slip into old habits when addressing her... Well, not that it matters. Whatever the case may be, she has dedicated herself to serving Fontaine for hundreds of years.

dialogues.speaker: Vimeur
dialogues.text: And even if she's not present, the trial will proceed without issues. You should have faith in the impartial judgments of our judges.
